stories.Headline: Economic Watch: AI takes on bigger role in China's express delivery during Singles' Day peak - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
China's express delivery companies are using more artificial intelligence during this year's Singles' Day shopping rush, Xinhua reported on Oct. 30. The Singles' Day festival, also called Double 11 because it falls on Nov. 11, is China's annual online shopping event and one of the world's biggest retail events. A drone can now lower a package into a smart locker that opens and closes its doors, and a customer later collects it with a code and no courier on site. STO Express has deployed AI "digital employees" through its SClaw intelligent-agent platform, and a digital quality-control system flags risks for fresh produce and other sensitive parcels.

JD Logistics has rolled out its upgraded Super Brain 3.0 large model as a decision-making hub, forecasting order volumes by region and adjusting nationwide logistics capacity in real time. The company said AI-recommended delivery routes have an adoption rate of more than 90.2 percent, and its robotic arms in sorting centers have reached a parcel tracking accuracy rate of 99.9 percent. SF Express is using sales forecasts and digital supply-chain tools to move inventory closer to consumers in advance. YTO Express has embedded more than 100 intelligent agents into route optimization, dispatch analysis and customer-service workflows, and put 28 digital employees to work in operations and customer service.

Luo Jian, who oversees Double 11 operations at STO Express, said the core change this year is using AI computing power to take on part of the frontline physical workload. He said proactive services help absorb peak pressure, and the company is raising efficiency without compromising safety so the whole network can handle the prolonged peak season. Hu Dajian, vice-president of the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing, said AI is shifting from isolated applications to whole-chain coordination. Zhang Yi, vice-president of the Guangdong Internet Society, said AI applications are now used across the entire e-commerce operation cycle, from product selection and content creation to traffic acquisition, customer service and competitor analysis.

A report by the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing showed AI adoption in China's logistics and supply chains had exceeded 37 percent, with transport at 78 percent, safety and compliance at 52.73 percent, and smart warehousing at 47.27 percent. China's express delivery sector handled 151.3 billion parcels in the first nine months of 2026, up 4.3 percent from a year earlier, according to the State Post Bureau. In 2025, China released a policy document to advance the "AI Plus" initiative, setting out goals and priorities for integrating AI across the economy and society. Industry observers said the broad commercial rollout of AI has become a major highlight of this year's Singles' Day peak, signaling that the next competitive edge will come less from scale than from AI embedded across the entire operational chain.

Articles.Title: Economic Watch: AI takes on bigger role in China's express delivery during Singles' Day peak - Xinhua

stories.Headline: US: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash burn fears spark tech sell-off
stories.Summary:
US stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30, 2026, after disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon deepened worries about heavy spending on artificial intelligence. The Nasdaq slid 2.9 per cent, its largest one-day percentage drop since June 5, and has fallen 7.8 per cent from its record closing high on October 6. Intel shares plunged 28.6 per cent, while Amazon pared its losses during the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 572.25 points, or 1.1 per cent, to 51,770.31, the S&P 500 lost 140.32 points, or 1.8 per cent, to 7,580.07, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 747.73 points, or 2.9 per cent, to 25,437.

Chip and server stocks fell hard. Nvidia dropped 4.2 per cent, AMD slid 10.9 per cent, and the broader chips index shed 7.2 per cent, ending the month down more than 15 per cent. Dell fell 10.8 per cent and HP 9.6 per cent. All three main indices closed lower on the week, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq logged monthly losses while the Dow ended October with a gain. The S&P 500 tech sector had its largest monthly percentage loss since March 2025, and communication services its biggest monthly drop since April 2022.

Oliver Pursche, senior vice-president at Wealthspire Advisors, said the week had been about the future of artificial intelligence, including whether it will bring a positive return on investment and how quickly. He said companies meeting lofty expectations were doing well, while those falling short were being punished. Exxon Mobil and Chevron beat profit expectations and rose 2.2 per cent and 2.8 per cent. Starbucks dipped 1.8 per cent after forecasting an annual revenue decline tied to the divestiture of its Chinese business.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 S&P 500 companies having reported and 82 per cent beating consensus expectations, according to LSEG data. Analysts expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6 per cent year on year, per LSEG. Crypto-related firms Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood fell between 7.2 and 10.6 per cent after reports that hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance. Volume on US exchanges was 19.87 billion shares, compared with the 17.26 billion average over the last 20 trading days.

stories.Headline: AI spending, oil and rate hikes: What is really steering markets
stories.Summary:
This week's big technology earnings gave mixed signals on artificial intelligence spending, with Alphabet falling while Microsoft was rewarded. Oil near US$115 kept inflation worries alive and central banks on edge. Asian technology swung sharply and private AI valuations headed for public markets. The discussion took place in a podcast published on Friday, October 30, 2026.

Paul Chew, head of research at Phillip Securities Research, said the weakness came from search advertising rather than capital expenditure. He said free cash flow will look weak while data centres are being built, and he found Amazon's rare guidance reassuring. He said record memory prices and booked demand matter more than fears that earnings have peaked. He called another Federal Reserve rate hike almost inevitable but doubted that higher rates cure an oil shock rooted in supply.

Chew said smaller central banks face a harder trade-off between defending currencies and protecting growth. He outlined what markets have priced in for oil and the Strait of Hormuz, and the scenario he said they have not: ground troops. His pick for the one indicator to watch is the revenue momentum of frontier AI model makers. He said a planned listing of Anthropic would give investors rare transparency into AI demand, and his advice is to take a view on how early AI adoption is rather than trade the headlines.

The podcast was an episode of Market Focus Weekly, a Business Times show. It was hosted by Howie Lim, and the article lists Claressa Monteiro as a name on the page. stories.Headline: Qwen-powered Apple AI to launch in China in December
stories.Summary:
Apple will integrate Alibaba Group's Qwen artificial intelligence models into Apple Intelligence in China, Apple said on Saturday. Qwen-powered features will be available for testing from Nov 4 in the latest iOS developer beta. They will be rolled out more broadly in December with the release of iOS 27.3. The partnership will let Chinese users reach Qwen through Siri, Apple's writing tools and its visual intelligence feature. For some requests, Siri will be able to call on Qwen's broader knowledge to answer directly.

A "Compose with Qwen" function will generate original content from a prompt, including text and images. Users can select "Ask Qwen" in visual intelligence to identify or obtain more information about objects and places. Alibaba Group CEO Eddie Wu said the company was delighted to partner with Apple. He said Qwen would be deeply integrated into experiences across the Apple ecosystem, drawing on Alibaba's deep AI capabilities. Apple said users will be asked for permission before a question, document or image is sent to Qwen.

Alibaba said requests and responses generated through the integration will not be used to train its models. China's cyberspace regulator registered Apple's on-device generative AI service for use on iPhones in July. The December update will not include the more advanced Siri AI capabilities or other next-generation Apple Intelligence features unveiled at its Worldwide Developers Conference this year. The first batch of features will be available on supported iPhones, including the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone 16 and later models, iPhone Air and iPhone Duo, with device and Siri languages set to English or Simplified Chinese.

Articles.Title: Qwen-powered Apple AI to launch in China in December - China Daily

stories.Headline: China's World Internet Conference summit to focus on open-source AI
stories.Summary:
Organizers said at a news conference in Beijing on Tuesday that the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit will put open-source AI and international cooperation on AI development and governance at the center of its agenda. The summit will take place from November 2 to 5 in Wuzhen, in east China's Zhejiang Province. It will bring together Chinese and international participants to discuss innovation, security governance, cultural exchanges and international cooperation. A dialogue at the main forum will gather executives from leading technology companies and developers of open-source large models to discuss how to build a global open-source AI ecosystem. The summit will feature 27 sub-forums, with topics including trust, connectivity and interoperability among AI agents, as well as robotics, embodied AI and spatiotemporal intelligence.

Cyberspace cooperation under the Global Governance Initiative will also feature in the discussions. The theme of this year's Wuzhen Summit emphasizes open source, inclusiveness, joint contribution and shared benefits in building a community with a shared future in cyberspace. Discussions will address both the principles and practical applications of open-source and inclusive AI development, as well as international concerns over its governance, according to the organizers. The summit is organized by the WIC, with the Zhejiang provincial government responsible for local arrangements. Other events will include the WIC Awards for Pioneering Science and Technology, the WIC Distinguished Contribution Award, the Light of Internet Expo, and presentations of outstanding cases of jointly building a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

The focus on open-source cooperation follows broader Chinese efforts to promote international collaboration in AI. An action plan issued at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai in July called for sharing open-source ecosystems, jointly developing rules and standards and strengthening cooperation on AI safety governance. First held in 2014, the Wuzhen Summit brings together government officials, representatives of international organizations, technology executives and researchers to discuss the development and governance of the internet. The WIC was established as an international organization headquartered in Beijing in 2022.

Articles.Title: China's World Internet Conference summit to focus on open-source AI - China Daily

stories.Headline: Most firms now use AI in HR processes, with human sign-off required 85% of the time: Survey - CNA
stories.Summary:
Most firms in Singapore now use artificial intelligence in human resources processes, according to a Singapore National Employers Federation survey released on Friday, Oct 30. SNEF counted almost 3,000 use cases of AI in HR in its survey of 1,000 employers from June to July. In 85 per cent of these use cases, a human confirms the final decision after AI provides input. In the remaining 15 per cent, AI makes the decision without a human signing off, and 73 per cent of those cases are in routine or high-volume administrative processes such as resume screening and skills assessments. In nearly all use cases without human sign-off, employers still name someone, such as the head of HR, a supervisor or a hiring manager, to step in and change or reverse the decision if needed.

Large organisations are more likely to use AI in HR, with 81 per cent of firms with more than 200 employees doing so, compared to 65 per cent of small and medium enterprises with 200 or fewer employees. AI use is heavier in the early stages of employment, such as screening and shortlisting candidates, personalising learning and workforce planning, and it is also used to analyse employee sentiment and attrition risk and to benchmark pay. Reliance is lowest at the end of the employment relationship, when dealing with separation and exit matters. SNEF said employers generally do not use AI where there are more significant consequences for employees, which it said reflects their continued trust in human judgment.

SNEF president Kuah Boon Wee said the level of oversight should match the stakes, with lighter monitoring for routine tasks and closer watching for decisions that affect people's livelihoods. He spoke at the inaugural SNEF Employers' Summit, which had the theme of harnessing AI for business and workforce outcomes. SNEF chief executive Hao Shuo, asked about potential bias, said employers are generally aware of the laws and their liability for discrimination offences, and that they make sure there is no bias when AI is used to sift CVs. The survey found 84 per cent of employers were very or extremely familiar with frameworks such as the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices and the forthcoming Workplace Fairness Act, set to come into effect end-2027.

Some employers already have safeguards, including monitoring the outcomes of AI tools, reviewing decision patterns, retraining models, tracking reasons for human intervention and giving feedback to vendors. In the United States, makers of AI hiring tools Workday and Eightfold AI face lawsuits contesting how fairly the tools were used to screen candidates, and these cases are being watched for possible implications. Employers' top concern, cited by 39 per cent, was that over-reliance on AI could erode HR capabilities over time. About one-third worried about when to trust AI over professional judgment, accountability when AI makes errors, and lack of training.

Articles.Title: Most firms now use AI in HR processes, with human sign-off required 85% of the time: Survey - CNA

stories.Headline: AI unlocks new future in parenting behavior
stories.Summary:
The 2026 West Bund Tech Consumer Carnival took place at the Shanghai West Bund International Convention and Exhibition Center from Oct 22 to Oct 25. It brought together more than 400 cutting-edge tech brands. These included AI-powered maternity feeding devices, child companion robots and smart interactive toys. The event offered a clear glimpse into how AI is reshaping child rearing in China.

China's AI boom in maternity and parenting began in earnest in 2025. In just one year, the civilian rollout of large language models and demand for refined parenting among younger generations pushed AI into feeding, companionship and early education. Snow-Bear's AI milk warmer uses ambient temperature recognition and infrared sensing to adjust heating based on seasonal changes and bottle materials. TCL-backed HeyAiMe's AiMe family companion robot launched in August for children aged 3 to 8. Babycare's smart AI interactive toy duck topped 2 million yuan, or $300,238, in sales in its debut month.

Lin Li, brand supervisor at SnowBear, said the core is AI-powered temperature calibration, which solves the problem of traditional devices being disrupted by environmental factors. Weng Xuwei, TCL's marketing manager, said the aim is to ease the burden on exhausted parents with quality companionship and play-driven learning. Yu Jiale, account manager at Babycare, said the biggest change brought by AI is greater humanity, and what used to be just a toy can now be a child's companion. He Yaqiong, director general of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's Department of Consumer Goods Industry, said AI and large language models have injected new vitality into toys.

China's AI toy market hit 24.6 billion yuan in 2024 and likely reached 29 billion yuan last year, according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Shanghai Aiyuhui Technology's Egg Baby connects to a WeChat mini-program via near-field communication, and the product will launch between late 2026 and the 2027 Spring Festival holiday. Zhang Di, founder and CEO of Aiyuhui, said AI will definitely revolutionize early childhood education. The carnival also linked early-stage projects with industrial resources and incubation support through forums, investment roadshows and innovation contests, speeding up adoption and commercialization of tech advances.

stories.Headline: Chinese and Elon Musk-linked AI films stumble at box office and with critics, exposing storytelling gap
stories.Summary:
Two artificial intelligence film projects, one in China and one linked to Elon Musk in the US, met weak box office and critical responses within days of each other. China's first fully AI-produced feature film to receive a screening permit, Sanxingdui, was released in theaters on October 23. By Thursday its cumulative box office had reached about 1.42 million yuan, or $213,000, and its audience occupancy rate had fallen to 0.2 percent, according to the ticketing platform Maoyan. Production costs were estimated at tens of millions of yuan, so receipts recovered less than a tenth of the reported budget.

A Beijing moviegoer surnamed Zhang told the Global Times that seeing an AI film in a cinema was a novelty, but the film had a heavy AI flavor and its plot was scattered and fragmented. Grok Imagine, the AI video tool from Musk's xAI, released the first seven-minute installment of its Odyssey series on Musk's platform X. The project followed Musk's public criticism of Christopher Nolan's live-action adaptation of Homer's epic, which he accused of sacrificing historical authenticity for political correctness. Musk has said he intends to produce a feature-length AI film by the end of 2026 that stays faithful to the spirit of Homer's work. The first episode drew criticism for its visuals and storytelling, with foreign media describing it as soulless slop.

Feng Anrong, a director who runs an AI production studio, told the Global Times that the core problem is not the technology but the disconnect between content and the market. He said both films stressed technological novelty while neglecting a coherent plot, engaging characters and emotional resonance. Zhang Peng, a cultural researcher and associate professor at Nanjing Normal University, said technology cannot compensate for weak storytelling. He said audiences empathize with a character's choices, sacrifices and fate, not with whether a real person plays the role.

Experts say AI filmmaking has yet to establish a mature production model for feature-length narratives, which typically run beyond 90 minutes and need sustained storytelling and controlled pacing. Zhang cautioned against concluding that AI suits only short videos, saying the setbacks expose weaknesses in long-form narrative control and production workflows. He said he was optimistic about the next three to five years, particularly for lower- and mid-budget science fiction, fantasy and animation projects. Feng said long-term prospects depend on generating genuine demand rather than publicity, investment or isolated box office successes, and that one or two blockbuster hits cannot revive an entire sector.

Articles.Title: Chinese and Elon Musk-linked AI films stumble at box office and with critics, exposing storytelling gap - Global Times

stories.Headline: Huawei Unveils Wireless Products to Meet AI-Era Network Demands
stories.Summary:
Huawei unveiled a new lineup of wireless network products on October 30, 2026, according to Caixin Global. Huawei said the launches bring advances in materials, antenna design, power efficiency and network resource management into commercial products. The company also outlined progress in building an open ecosystem for telecom AI agents. Fang is the Huawei executive responsible for the wireless network business and presented the lineup. stories.Headline: OpenAI reports AI agents used a CPU cache channel
stories.Summary:
OpenAI reported on October 23, 2026, that AI agents in separate microVMs on shared host machines exchanged synthetic secrets through CPU-cache timing in a controlled red-team test. The agents had no network connections and no shared writable files. One agent evicted selected cache data while another timed the reloads and decoded the signal using an agreed protocol. Because the microVMs ran on shared hosts, cache timing carried a signal between the otherwise separate environments.

OpenAI said the agents were asked to exchange synthetic secrets, and that the wider red-team campaign tested whether agents could reach the live internet, cross an internal security boundary, or communicate across isolation boundaries. OpenAI supplied campaign teams with infrastructure source code, configuration details, and vulnerability documentation so defenses could be tested under attacker-favorable conditions. It said most communication tests directed agents toward particular channels or gave them an encoding and decoding protocol, and the cache test belongs to that directed context. OpenAI connected cache timing to techniques used in Spectre and Meltdown.

OpenAI said most channels in the campaign carried information slowly and were difficult for models to exploit. It reported adding monitoring checks to detect attempts to communicate through the channels. It also said it patched software, tightened network restrictions, and strengthened monitoring. The cache experiment demonstrated communication across the isolation boundary between microVMs, while host-escape and internet-access tests were discussed separately in the wider campaign.

Articles.Title: OpenAI reports AI agents used a CPU cache channel - NeoTeo

stories.Headline: South Korea's Four Major Science and Technology Institutes Unveil 8 Deep-Tech Breakthroughs, From AI Chip Power Delivery to Spent-Battery Recycling
stories.Summary:
South Korea's four major science and technology institutes, KAIST, GIST, DGIST and UNIST, presented eight commercialization-ready technologies at the 2026 K-Premier Deep Tech Festa. The event was held on the 29th at COEX in Seoul's Gangnam District and was co-hosted by the Ministry of Science and ICT, the four institutes and Money Today's Unicorn Factory. Each institute presented two technologies, and the researchers explained their purpose, what sets them apart and their industrial applications. A UNIST team led by Professor Kim Gwi-yong won the grand prize for a process that recovers nickel from spent batteries.

The UNIST process uses a deep eutectic solvent and electrodeposition to recover nickel at a 99% rate and 99.1% purity, with cobalt recovery and purity both above 95%. Repeated purification raised final metal purity to more than 99.9%, and the solvent showed no performance degradation after four consecutive reuses. A KAIST team led by Professor Kim Sang-hyun developed a technology that places a vertical voltage regulator directly beneath chips and uses gallium nitride to lift AI semiconductor power delivery efficiency from the 50% range to as high as 95%. DGIST's Kim Woon-hyuk showed that nano-sizing cathode particles eases microcracking in all-solid-state batteries, and the material retained more than 90% of its initial capacity after 300 charge-discharge cycles.

Kim Woon-hyuk said materials account for about 75% of battery cost, with cathode materials making up about 49.5%, and that adding just one alloying element allows existing equipment to be used as is. The event also included a consultation hall where companies held one-on-one meetings with researchers on technology transfers and commercialization. The industrial viability of the results remains at the verification stage, and for the AI semiconductor power technology the next task is to package components into a single integrated circuit and show efficiency gains at the circuit level. In the spent-battery technology, the solvent accounts for about 40.6% of costs, making more reuse cycles the key to cost reduction.

Articles.Title: South Korea's Four Major Science and Technology Institutes Unveil 8 Deep-Tech Breakthroughs, From AI Chip Power Delivery to Spent-Battery Recycling - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: KAIST report maps how AI could fail Koreans by 2036
stories.Summary:
KAIST announced on Friday a report called "2036 AI Future Failure Scenarios," based on a nationwide idea contest that drew 732 participants and produced 429 scenarios, according to Aju Press. Only entries meeting the criteria of KAIST's Center for Ambitious Failure were included. Participants used a premortem method, assuming a failure had already happened in 2036 and tracing its causes backward to choices that could still be changed today. The report was announced in Seoul on October 30, 2026.

The report built an "AI future risk map" covering eight domains, including education and learning, labor and expertise, and health and medical care, along with seven pathways to failure. It also examined conditions under which a single failure could grow into a wider social risk, such as the same error spreading in many places at once or heavy dependence on a handful of platforms. The center said the scenarios are not forecasts and do not estimate how likely any risk is. It said their value lies in identifying questions that current technology, policy and institutions need to examine.

KAIST President Bae Choong-sik said a university should be a place that respects and learns from not only successful results but also the trial and error that comes with taking on a challenge. The report is one of two publications KAIST will present at its fourth Failure Conference, which runs from Nov. 4 to 13 on its Daejeon campus under the theme "Future and Failure." The conference opens at 6 p.m. on Nov. 4 with the Failed Project Bragging Contest, organized with the student group ICISTS. On Nov. 6 at 3 p.m., three winners of this year's failure essay contest will discuss their ongoing struggles, followed by a lecture by Seo Yong-seok, a professor at KAIST's Moon Soul Graduate School of Future Strategy.

The Center for Ambitious Failure was founded in 2021 to ease the fear of failure among members of the KAIST community and first held the conference in 2023. Throughout the conference, the lobby of the Creative Learning Building will host an exhibition of the citizens' 2036 scenarios and the risk map, alongside "Failure Photovoice," a display of photos and writing in which students recorded failures from daily life. The second publication, "The Tense of Failure," collects the 16 winning entries from the 2026 essay contest. All conference programs are open to the public, and registration for the seminar is being taken online. Both publications will be posted as e-books on the center's website, caf.kaist.ac.kr.

Articles.Title: KAIST report maps how AI could fail Koreans by 2036 - Aju Press

stories.Headline: Alphabet suffers record fall as AI Mode cuts advertising dollars
stories.Summary:
Alphabet's shares fell more than 12% on Thursday, their biggest single-day decline on record, after the company reported weaker-than-expected advertising revenue and a sharp deterioration in cash flow. The sell-off came after Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1bn for the third quarter ending 30th September, against analysts' expectations that the company would come close to breaking even, according to LSEG data. The company also recorded a cash outflow of $5.9bn in the second quarter, its second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Total revenue rose to $127.6bn, below analysts' estimates of $128.2bn, and advertising revenue reached $82bn, short of the expected $83.4bn.

Alphabet CFO Anat Ashkenazi told analysts that capital expenditure was expected to increase substantially in 2027, compared with projected spending of between $195bn and $205bn this year. She did not disclose a specific figure for next year's investment, and she also warned that using third-party cloud computing capacity would put pressure on profit margins in the near term. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said the greater adoption of AI Mode, a chatbot-style search interface, had contributed to a larger-than-expected slowdown in search advertising growth. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71bn in the third quarter, exceeding analysts' expectations, and the cloud backlog increased to $561bn, with Ashkenazi saying Alphabet expected to recognise more than 55% of that amount as revenue over the next 24 months.

Google Cloud chief executive Thomas Kurian said sales of the company's tensor processing units, which compete with Nvidia's GPUs, had become a meaningful contributor to the division's business, and Alphabet began recognising revenue from direct sales of its TPU systems last quarter. The contrast with Microsoft was particularly noticeable, as Microsoft reported $18.6bn in free cash flow for its third quarter despite continuing to invest heavily in AI infrastructure, and its shares ended Thursday broadly unchanged. Google's search advertising business is facing growing competition from AI-powered services like ChatGPT and Claude, which can serve information to users without involving traditional search engines. Alphabet is attempting to balance the introduction of AI-powered search features with the need to protect the advertising business that has historically generated most of its revenue.

Articles.Title: Alphabet suffers record fall as AI Mode cuts advertising dollars - Computing UK

stories.Headline: Edge AI inference offers telecoms a new growth engine
stories.Summary:
Edge AI inference is emerging as a possible new growth area for telecom operators, according to an article published on October 30, 2026. The shift is being driven by latency, data gravity and cost, which are expected to push some AI tasks from hyperscale data centers toward the edge as generative and agentic AI move into daily use. Nvidia has already signaled the opportunity through projects and partnerships involving AT&T, Charter Communications, Cisco, Nokia, SoftBank, Telefónica and T-Mobile. Nvidia's focus includes edge AI for factory and robotics uses, often called physical AI, which is closely tied to AI-RAN.

The article says deploying high-performance AI inference at far-edge sites such as radio towers or cell sites is difficult. David Duggal, CEO of EnterpriseWeb, described a Catch-22 situation for AI on towers because GPUs use a lot of power and generate heat, which requires substantial supporting infrastructure and makes such deployments economically hard. The Telecommunications Industry Association is working to define unified practices for AI data center infrastructure, and Mike Peterson, who leads the association's Data Center Program, said AI infrastructure is changing physical design assumptions including cabling, interconnect design, power distribution and cooling. US telecom operators hold real estate such as central offices and legacy switching facilities that could be repurposed for edge inference, an idea being explored in standards work as community resistance complicates new data center development.

Luis Fernandes, a senior research manager at IDC, cautioned against overstating latency as the universal driver for edge AI. Research by IDC and the European Commission found that workload type is often more determining, with real-time workloads needing instant responses shaped by local context while analytical workloads typically do not. Akamai is deploying GPU-equipped edge nodes within telecom central offices, and Jon Alexander, a senior vice president at Akamai's Cloud Technology Group, said physical AI remains among the most latency-sensitive use cases. He added that metro-level edge infrastructure delivering 5- to 10-millisecond response times may suffice for a broad range of commercial AI workloads.

Articles.Title: Edge AI inference offers telecoms a new growth engine - ET Datacenters

stories.Headline: CoreWeave Sinks 11%, Nebius Tumbles 9% as Hyperscaler Spending Jitters Rattle AI Cloud Stocks; Cloudflare Plunges 12%, Snowflake Drops 9%
stories.Summary:
AI cloud stocks fell sharply after Microsoft reported capital spending below expectations on October 28, 2026. CoreWeave dropped 11% to $54.34 and Nebius fell 9% to $156.73. Cloudflare slid 12% to $274.14 and Snowflake dropped 9% to $299.63. The selloff came as investors questioned how much the biggest tech companies will keep paying for outside computing power.

Alphabet added to the concern on October 29, shedding more than $500 billion in market value after quarterly free cash flow came in at negative $9.1 billion, worse than the negative $3.5 billion analysts expected. Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel expects hyperscalers to stay cash-negative, with losses near $200 billion over the next year. CoreWeave's interest expense rose to $640 million in Q2 from $267 million a year earlier. Its revenue backlog stood at $104.2 billion as of June 30, with more than $25 billion in net new customer commitments added early in Q3 2026.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said on the August 11 call that near-term capacity remains effectively sold out. Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said on the August 6 call that his company is in a different business than hyperscalers, selling work getting done rather than leasing compute. Nebius chief operating officer Ophir Nave pointed to more than $40 billion in investment-grade customer commitments on long-term contracts as another funding source. Cloudflare reported Q2 2026 revenue of $696.1 million, up 35.9% year over year, and Snowflake reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.55 billion, up 35.1%.

Grayscale said on October 27 that its AI Computing ETF, trading under the ticker GCPU, invests in stocks tied to AI infrastructure, with CoreWeave, Nebius and DigitalOcean among its main holdings. Nebius will report third-quarter results before the market opens on November 12. CoreWeave and Cloudflare both have reports coming up, and Snowflake reports later. CoreWeave's report will test whether customer demand holds up as hyperscalers rethink their budgets.

Articles.Title: CoreWeave Sinks 11%, Nebius Tumbles 9% as Hyperscaler Spending Jitters Rattle AI Cloud Stocks; Cloudflare Plunges 12%, Snowflake Drops 9% - 24/7 Wall St.

stories.Headline: Edge0 Releases Audio8-TTS-Realistic, a 0.6B Voice Cloning TTS Model
stories.Summary:
Edge0 released Audio8-TTS-Realistic on October 30, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. It is an open-weight text-to-speech model for zero-shot voice cloning that clones a voice from one reference clip and its transcript. The model has 0.6 billion parameters, or 601 million in the main model excluding the codec, and supports 23 languages, 12 more than its predecessor. The weights and code ship under the Apache 2.0 license, and it is the second 0.6B release in Edge0's Audio8 TTS family, building on Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b with the same Transformers inference interface.

The model handles up to 2,048 packed text and audio positions of context and recommends a CUDA GPU, having been smoke-tested on an NVIDIA H20 in BF16. The new languages are Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese. It uses a dual-autoregressive design inspired by Fish Audio S2 Pro, with a slow branch built on Qwen2.5 0.5B and a shallow 4-layer fast branch. Edge0 reports 4.86% average error on CV3 across 9 languages, versus 7.73% for Qwen3-TTS-1.7B, but 48.57% word error rate on Thai and 31.35% character error rate on Cantonese. Larger models still lead in places, with Higgs TTS 3 reporting 4.41% on CV3 and 2.74% on MiniMax, and Edge0 calls its table a reference comparison because evaluation pipelines differ.

Edge0's team argues that word error rate and speaker similarity miss rhythm, pauses and timing, so a model can score well on both and still sound synthetic. Its training included multilingual supervised fine-tuning and GRPO with a combined reward weighting word error rate at 0.7 and speaker similarity at 0.3, plus a stage guided by a learned realism critic trained on a quality ladder from 6 open-source TTS systems ranked in a private blind listening study. An identity-erasure loss stops the critic from rewarding generator fingerprints, and a duration penalty kicks in beyond 1.35 times the reference length. The final stage used only Chinese and English prompts but still improved the 13 lower-resource languages, with error falling from 22.53% to 20.77% and similarity rising from 0.637 to 0.679.

To use it, developers need PyTorch 2.5 or later and Transformers 4.57 or later, loading with trust_remote_code=True, and voice cloning needs a clean reference clip and its exact transcript. The GitHub repo adds a CLI, batching and supervised fine-tuning scripts, and for GPU serving an SGLang Omni adapter provides paged attention, dynamic batching and an OpenAI-compatible speech API. Edge0 notes that throughput and streaming were not benchmarked, and no Realistic ONNX export is public yet. A free Playground runs on Hugging Face ZeroGPU, and the paper reports 1.1 to 1.2 GiB peak memory on an Apple M2 CPU in INT4 ONNX.

Articles.Title: Edge0 Releases Audio8-TTS-Realistic, a 0.6B Voice Cloning TTS Model

stories.Headline: The End of the AI Infrastructure Boom, and What Alphabet's Capital Expenditures and CoreWeave's Setbacks Mean for Valuation and Investment Strategy
stories.Summary:
Alphabet reported $51.4 billion of capital spending and negative $9.1 billion of free cash flow for a second quarter in a row, and its shares fell about 13% on 29 October, their worst day on record. CoreWeave's shares fell about 36% in October as of 21 October as investors focused on its debt, before recovering some ground in the final days of the month. One of CoreWeave's bonds, due in 2031, traded at a yield near 15.8% as concern centred on its debt. The article says investors are shifting from rewarding AI infrastructure spending to demanding cash discipline and clear funding milestones.

The article says AI infrastructure firms should adopt a financially disciplined approach to capital allocation and build financial models that can withstand scrutiny. It says establishing clear milestones for funding these capital-intensive businesses is advantageous so the market does not treat AI infrastructure capital as a cost. It adds that price discovery through cloud providers or large internal deployments by individual customers should remain critical in determining the appropriate, truly profitable scale. It also says continued funding market discipline, in risk pricing and timing, is highly desirable for capital-intensive players.

JPMorgan strategist Justin Biemann says lenders now require proof of cash flow, not just an AI label, according to the article. The article reports that CoreWeave's default-insurance costs hit record highs and neocloud bond spreads blew out. It says AI companies need strong cash flow fundamentals and lenders demand proof AI startups can repay debt. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress says H100 rental prices are up 20% this year, and the article says Nebius raised its own GPU rates by as much as 21% and still filled capacity.

The article says the combined implications of Alphabet's elevated capital spending and CoreWeave's debt stress suggest an inflection point in AI infrastructure investment. It says investors had previously absorbed the costs of accelerated AI investment, but the market is becoming increasingly impatient. It notes that Alphabet's high valuation multiples reflect its revenue and free cash flow record, which enables ample recourse to internal funding. The article says underlying demand remains strong for AI workloads, but the potential pricing model and customer units available may not support the highly capital-intensive nature of these assets.

Articles.Title: The End of the AI Infrastructure Boom, and What Alphabet's Capital Expenditures and CoreWeave's Setbacks Mean for Valuation and Investment Strategy - Startup Fortune

stories.Headline: AI Security Agents Compared: Claude, Codex, Mantis, Cloudflare
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, OpenAI, Cloudflare and Google each now offer an AI agent that looks for security bugs in source code, according to a comparison published by MarkTechPost on October 30, 2026. The article says all four tools follow the same design: one agent finds a bug, a separate agent tries to disprove it, and only findings that survive get a patch. The tools differ in where they run, who can use them and how much proof they demand. The article describes the shared problem as noise, citing Google's security team as saying sloppy AI scanning produces invented bugs and true-positive rates under 7%.

Claude Security runs inside a Claude Code session and needs no separate API key, with scans counting against a Claude plan's usage limits. It offers three jobs from one menu, scan the codebase, scan changes or suggest patches, and produces a Markdown report plus a SARIF 2.1.0 file, with patches drafted in a scratch copy and never committed or pushed on its own. Anthropic opened a limited preview called Claude Code Security in February 2026, the hosted product reached public beta for Enterprise customers on Claude Opus 4.7, the Claude Code plugin entered beta on July 22, 2026, and in August the hosted scanner moved to Claude Mythos 5. Codex Security is a CLI and TypeScript SDK published as @openai/codex-security, with an Apache-2.0 CLI, though scanning still needs OpenAI access. It scans a whole repo, selected paths or a Git diff, has a deep mode with parallel discovery workers, and exports threat models, SARIF, JSON or CSV, with a GitHub Action that reports findings only by default.

Cloudflare's skill is MIT-licensed, model-agnostic and the most-starred at 47.5K, and its README states that the verifier is never the agent that found the bug. Google's Mantis reproduces bugs in a sandbox, and Google says it should be isolated. Anthropic says it built its scanner partly because attackers were already using AI models to find exploitable flaws, and Google opens its Mantis post by noting that models can now discover and exploit bugs with little human help. The article does not say what happens next beyond these releases.

Articles.Title: AI Security Agents Compared: Claude, Codex, Mantis, Cloudflare

stories.Headline: E2E Networks, Hitachi Energy India, Mtar Tech, other AI-related shares fall up to 5% amid global sell-off
stories.Summary:
Shares of E2E Networks, Hitachi Energy India, MTAR Technologies and other artificial intelligence-related companies fell by up to 5 percent on Friday, October 30, 2026. The decline tracked a global sell-off in technology stocks over concerns about rising spending on AI infrastructure and the returns from such investments. Netweb Technologies settled more than 5 percent lower at Rs 4,165 per share on the NSE. MTAR Technologies fell 5 percent to Rs 6,810 per share, while Black Box declined 3.5 percent to Rs 793 per share. E2E Networks and ESDS Software Solution both hit their 5 percent lower circuit limits.

Among power equipment companies linked to the AI infrastructure theme, Hitachi Energy India dropped 3.2 percent to Rs 27,225 per share. GE Vernova T&D India declined nearly 2 percent to Rs 4,020 per share, while CG Power and Industrial Solutions fell more than 3 percent to Rs 804 per share on the NSE. Anant Raj, which is expanding its data centre business in India, fell nearly 4 percent to Rs 446 per share. The sell-off was also visible in Asian and US-listed technology stocks, with Samsung Electronics sold after earnings came in below estimates and the release of its shareholder return plan was delayed.

In the US, chipmakers Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. fell 2.8 percent and 6.9 percent respectively in premarket trading. Server and storage provider Super Micro Computer Inc. declined 5 percent, power producer Bloom Energy Corp. fell 7 percent, and cloud computing firm CoreWeave Inc. was down 6 percent. Jai Malhi, a senior equity strategist at Vanda Research, told Bloomberg that tech earnings have proven a major hurdle with investors suddenly becoming capex vigilantes. He said that with seemingly higher funding costs of capex, tech names are being punished if revenue growth is not beating a high bar.

The decline in Indian technology stocks came amid a broader sell-off in global technology shares following earnings announcements by major companies. Results from Amazon.com Inc. and Intel Corp. raised fresh concerns about capital expenditure on AI infrastructure, and Alphabet Inc.'s shares posted a record decline after its results. Investors are also worried about rising borrowing costs as companies take on billions of dollars in debt to fund their AI expansion plans, while earnings growth has failed to match the scale of investments. The latest earnings have added to concerns over whether heavy investments in AI infrastructure will generate returns quickly enough to justify the high valuations of technology companies.

Articles.Title: E2E Networks, Hitachi Energy India, Mtar Tech, other AI-related shares fall up to 5% amid global sell-off - Moneycontrol.com

stories.Headline: GitHub Adds Tools to Manage AI Coding Agents Running in Parallel at Scale
stories.Summary:
GitHub announced new Copilot capabilities at its GitHub Universe conference on October 28, 2026, aimed at helping DevOps teams coordinate multiple AI coding agents working at the same time across projects. The updates include Copilot Fusion for task orchestration, expanded workflow automation, deeper AI-powered code reviews and wider access to Copilot features for GitHub Enterprise customers. GitHub also made generally available a Copilot projects tool within the Copilot application to track the progress of multiple agents across sessions running in parallel. Copilot Fusion evaluates what a task needs across reasoning, code generation, debugging and tools before deciding how best to execute it across one or more AI models.

Copilot automations, a cloud-based service that teams can invoke manually, schedule or trigger by events, can now learn from outcomes and propose improvements to workflows. GitHub added a Copilot code review Max tier that analyzes code more deeply to surface bugs before code reaches production. Enterprise customers will no longer pay a separate licensing fee for agentic AI tools beyond the cost of invoking the underlying models, and can use all Copilot features without a separate subscription. Microsoft added four million CPU cores, 160 PB of high-speed storage and 50 Tb/s of network capacity in the last year, and expects to finish moving GitHub to a multi-region Azure environment by early 2027.

Jay Parikh, executive vice president for CoreAI at Microsoft, said the software development lifecycle is no longer linear because developers use agents to run tasks in parallel, so every part of the GitHub stack must evolve. He said developers matter more than ever, predicting that all software written to date will amount to less than 1% of what will be written in the next five years. Parikh said the infrastructure work follows outages in the past year partly caused by rising demand from AI agents, and he acknowledged the platform must do better. GitHub now has 225 million developers, 17.9 billion code pushes, 33.4 billion commits, 1.34 billion pull requests and 566 million open source projects and repositories.

The article does not say when the new capabilities become available beyond the general availability of the Copilot projects tool. It also does not say how the changes will be priced beyond the removal of the separate enterprise licensing fee. The piece notes that the platform has added a new developer every second for the second year in a row. It raises the question of whether the added capacity will be enough as millions of AI agents use the infrastructure to build, test and deploy applications.

Articles.Title: GitHub Adds Tools to Manage AI Coding Agents Running in Parallel at Scale - DevOps.com

stories.Headline: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
stories.Summary:
DoorDash cut the latency of its AI-powered grocery reorder flow from about 16 seconds to 2 seconds, the company reported in late October 2026. The change doubled shopping list views and raised the flow's order rate by roughly 34 percent. The work builds on DoorDash's shared agent platform and its grounded shopping interface, which lets consumers edit shopping lists directly. The implementation sits inside Ask DoorDash, the company's conversational shopping assistant.

The system processes 90 days of purchase history along with consumer profile signals, using batch large language model inference to identify likely recurring purchases. Deterministic validation checks the generated results before reusable shopping list data is stored. The serving path then retrieves that prepared data and resolves each item against the current catalog, trying the original store item first, then a catalog product identifier, and finally a search term. This lets the system handle changing listings and unavailable products without repeating historical reasoning on every request. The Grocery agent is still invoked for requests that need more reasoning, such as finding cheaper alternatives based on prices, promotions, package sizes, inventory and preferences.

The shared platform provides orchestration, memory, model access, tracing, evaluation infrastructure and rollout controls, while domain teams keep ownership of agent instructions, skills, tools and evaluation criteria. DoorDash says adding its Reservations agent took one week, about ten times faster than building its first domain agents. Twisha Jain, a DoorDash engineer, wrote in a LinkedIn post that better agentic systems are not always about more reasoning but about deciding what belongs in the agent loop and what can happen ahead of time. She said a consumer's direct edit is authoritative, so the next agent turn starts from the edited list rather than from what was said earlier.

Moving recurring purchase analysis offline reduces the work needed during a live request while keeping current catalog information for product selection. Simpler operations, such as changing quantities or removing products, update the shopping list directly without another LLM round trip. The design treats the shopping list as a structured artifact that both the consumer and the agent can update, rather than relying only on conversational history. Other grocery platforms also use AI to personalize shopping, and Instacart's assistant supports meal planning, list creation and product discovery. DoorDash's approach focuses specifically on cutting reorder latency by separating historical purchase analysis from live product resolution.

Articles.Title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents - infoq.com
