stories.Headline: 5 Spooky Things About Trusting AI with Reliability
stories.Summary:
In August, Reuters reported on internal Meta posts showing what happened as the company pushed its engineers toward AI tooling. Code changes to internal platforms rose 220% year over year, while changes that actually reached users rose 36%. Major technical and security incidents rose 40%, and the time engineers spent firefighting them rose 70%. Meta declined to comment on those figures.

The article says AI writes code faster than anyone can review it. New Relic's 2026 State of AI Coding report found that 62% of technology leaders say their teams often ship AI-generated code to production without line-by-line verification. It also found that 95% of organizations allow vibe coding for production services, and none ban it outright. In the same report, 94% of respondents rate AI-generated code as higher quality than human-written code at review. Yet 78% report more incidents once it ships, and 82% have hit at least one production failure tied to AI-generated code in the past six months.

Kolton Andrus, CEO of the experimentation platform Gremlin, wrote the article. He argues that AI learns how systems are supposed to work, not how they fail, and that it cannot see your production or prove its own fix. He says none of this is a reason to slow down, and that teams should use AI aggressively while keeping their engineering discipline. He calls for reliability guardrails, including automated checks in the pipeline and making failure behavior the release bar. He describes Foresight AI, whose supervised agents are grounded in the Failure Atlas, a record built from more than ten years of resilience testing.

The article says teams are already giving AI a lot of trust and doing very little verification. It says trust is earned slowly and lost in a single outage, and that AI has not earned it yet. It says every fix AI suggests needs proof until then. It ends by saying reliability works the same way as Halloween, and that teams should find the failures before they find their customers.

Articles.Title: 5 Spooky Things About Trusting AI with Reliability - SD Times

stories.Headline: Sweet launches virtual patching for cloud & AI workloads
stories.Summary:
Sweet Security launched Virtual Patching for running cloud and AI workloads, the company announced on 31 October 2026. The feature is designed to help security teams block exploitation of known vulnerabilities before permanent fixes are deployed. It targets the gap between the discovery of a software flaw and the point at which engineering teams can test and release a code fix into production. Security teams can identify a vulnerability in Sweet's catalogue, choose an enforcement option and deploy a policy to nodes running the affected workload.

Sweet's sensor then applies the policy to the live application and blocks requests that attempt to exploit the weakness, while allowing normal traffic to continue. The protection remains attached to the workload as it scales or restarts and can be removed once the permanent fix is in place. The feature also links with Sweet Attack, the company's autonomous AI red-team agent, which continuously validates exploitable attack paths using runtime context from live environments. When it identifies a vulnerability, it can suggest a virtual patching policy for immediate enforcement.

Dror Kashti, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Sweet Security, said the product is intended to shorten the time between identifying an exposure and acting on it. He said that when a team knows an application can be exploited, waiting is not an option, and that the feature lets security teams protect production immediately while engineering finishes the permanent fix. James Berthoty, Chief Executive Officer and Founder of Latio Tech, said AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploitation to the point where exploits emerge days before patches are available. He said faster patching alone is not enough and that virtual patching provides a critical layer of protection against known and unknown exploits.

The launch comes as security teams face shorter timelines between disclosure and attempted exploitation of software vulnerabilities. Sweet pointed to a recent Atlassian flaw that drew exploitation attempts within hours of a proof of concept becoming public, while many software fixes still take days or weeks to reach production systems. Sweet said its virtual patching approach is available for cloud and AI applications running in production and is intended to work while engineering teams continue with standard remediation processes. The company said its sensor blocks exploit attempts against the targeted vulnerability while leaving normal requests unaffected.

Articles.Title: Sweet launches virtual patching for cloud & AI workloads - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Meet TokenEconomizer: Microsoft’s Plugin That Cuts Coding Agent Costs by Up to 30.9%
stories.Summary:
A team of researchers from Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley released TokenEconomizer, an open-source cost controller for coding agents, according to a report published on October 30, 2026. It is a plugin that learns from past sessions in a repository to cut waste in later ones. It works with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi, and it does not touch model weights or agent code. On 277 SWE-Bench tasks, it lowered mean cost by 18.4% to 30.9% across 5 agent-model settings.

The package is a standard-library Python package with agent plugins and 3 switchable mechanisms. It runs on any machine with Python 3.10 or higher and needs no GPU and no API key of its own. The best result was 30.9% lower cost on Claude Code with Opus 4.8, or 33.2% when combined with RTK. The smallest savings were 6.4% to 9.3% on ReposVul audits, and Pass@1 dropped 1.0 point on Opus 4.8. Pass@1 improved in 4 of 5 settings, and costs also fell 16.0% to 21.2% on Web-Bench and 16.5% to 19.6% on CredData.

The researchers profiled 60 SWE-Bench tasks across 6 repositories using Claude Code with Opus 4.8 and found 3 recurring sources of waste. Repeated discovery meant that once 5 tasks preceded the current one, 30% of tool calls repeated an earlier action. Of 23 tool schemas loaded every turn, 16 were never called and 3 covered 98% of calls. Ten failed runs were 17% of tasks but 32% of total spend. The team said TokenEconomizer treats the agent as a black box and keeps a state per repository built from completed traces, setting 3 policies before each task through the prompt, the tool settings and the event stream.

An LLM proposer turns trace digests into one-line facts, and a fact enters the prompt after 3 confirmations on tasks with non-overlapping edited files, with its need rate staying at or above 0.4. One contradiction counts as 5 confirmations, so wrong facts retire quickly. Shell, read, write and edit tools are always kept, while other tools are masked after 3 consecutive unused tasks or when an LLM judge marks them irrelevant, and the full catalog returns every 5 tasks. The controller learns a turn budget of 1.25 times the 90th percentile of successful run lengths, and a stuck agent gets 1 redirect, then a stop if the loop recurs. Savings build over time, and most repositories cost more at first but all were cheaper by the sixth task.

Articles.Title: Meet TokenEconomizer: Microsoft’s Plugin That Cuts Coding Agent Costs by Up to 30.9%

stories.Headline: Zoom pushes AI tools to drive work from talk to tasks
stories.Summary:
Zoom used its Zoomtopia APAC 2026 event on 30 October 2026 to outline new artificial intelligence features and a strategy it calls a system of action, meant to help users move from conversation to task completion. Executives set out how Zoom is expanding beyond meetings and communications into workflow support, customer service and follow-up tasks. The programme was organised around three areas, Conversation, Context and Completion, with demonstrations of note-taking, search, transcription and customer support tools. Carlos Quaderi, Head of APAC at Zoom, opened the event by highlighting regional activity, including the launch of Zoom Contact Centre in India and AI work in South Korea and Australia.

The first part of the framework covered communication tools, including meeting updates such as Touch up My Voice, Voice Translator and a planned Live Assist function, plus chat changes such as clearer threads and smarter filtering. The second part centred on context, with My Notes, designed to preserve meeting context and provide transcription across platforms and for in-person meetings, along with enriched meeting notes and Agentic search. The third part dealt with completion, including Zoom Virtual Agent Kiosk for physical locations and a headless approach to Zoom's Unified Context Layer, with new MCP server connections for external tools including Claude. Zoom also said it already uses a federated AI approach that brings together more than one model.

Eric Yuan, Chief Executive Officer of Zoom, described the company's shift from a platform focused on conversations to one intended to support the actions that follow them, and said the goal is to consolidate what have often been two-step workflows into single actions. He said Zoom aims to support multiple models while maintaining security, governance and compliance. Angela Jiang of Anthropic said effective agents need access to knowledge bases, embedded institutional knowledge and memory for more accurate responses and task handling. Christine Sarros of Oracle said the company had scaled its use of Zoom tools to more than 10,000 agents globally while meeting security and compliance requirements, and Christian Wilson of First Bank said the bank implemented Zoom's portfolio in 100 days across 11 operations teams.

Zoom presented Oracle as its largest customer in North America, with an 11-year relationship. The event also included a demonstration of how the unified context layer can connect information from different departments and channels, with one support scenario identifying repeated docking station failures across several customer cases. Nayeema Raza introduced the theme "From Conversation to Completion", and Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman spoke about decision-making in high-pressure environments. The article says the emphasis on context, action and follow-through reflects a wider push among workplace software groups to tie generative AI tools more closely to daily tasks, and that for Zoom the next stage of competition will centre on whether software can carry work through to an outcome.

Articles.Title: Zoom pushes AI tools to drive work from talk to tasks - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Australian AI firms test Singapore market opportunities
stories.Summary:
Austrade and the Tech Council of Australia took 24 Australian AI companies to Singapore to test commercial opportunities, the delegation held more than 100 engagements with prospective customers, partners and industry stakeholders. The mission brought together companies working across digital infrastructure, enterprise AI, governance, cyber security and sector-specific applications to gauge demand in a market moving from AI experimentation to wider deployment. More than 60 of the engagements were scheduled business-matching meetings. Further discussions took place through an AI forum, a Team Australia pavilion and activities around Singapore Tech Week. The trip was backed by the Australian Government's Accessing New Markets Initiative and formed part of a broader trade diversification effort led by Austrade and industry groups.

Three themes emerged from the meetings and events, buyers are looking for measurable business value rather than AI experimentation, and trust, governance and security remain central to adoption decisions. Demand is also rising for enabling infrastructure such as compute capacity and sovereign cloud services. The AI Transformation Forum, held during the visit, focused on what organisations need to move AI from early trials into day-to-day operations. Speakers from government and industry said large-scale deployment depends on clear business priorities, leadership commitment, workforce capability, and trusted data and governance foundations. The event featured contributions from AI Singapore, OpenAI, Google Cloud, Mastercard and SJ Group, alongside Australian businesses, and Australia's Deputy High Commissioner to Singapore, Emily Follett, opened the forum.

Dr Kate Cornick, Chief Executive Officer of the Tech Council of Australia, said that for some companies this is their first entry into the Asian market, while others are looking to grow their existing footprint. She said Singapore offers enormous opportunities for Australian tech companies as a landing pad into Asia regardless of where they are on that journey. Tsubasa Bolt, Deputy Director, Sustainable Assets and Climate Solutions at SJ Group, said the advantage of AI will come from the effectiveness of its deployment, not from access. Kenn Rodrigues, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of DHI, said the meetings helped identify possible local partners and that customers are looking for solutions built around a defined use case, supported by partners who understand the local market. He said the business-matching helped identify several potential partners and that the next step is to continue those discussions and assess where there is the strongest fit.

The Australian delegation included Sharon AI, SCX.ai and XENON Systems in AI infrastructure, compute and secure deployment, alongside Nuix, DTEX, Vericent, IDmeta and ViewDS in governance, compliance, risk management and digital trust. Other delegates, including Mentana, Priori Analytica, FortifyEdge and ResQVision, focused on applications in supply chains, agribusiness, critical infrastructure, energy optimisation, public safety and industrial operations. Austrade sees Singapore as a practical route into wider Southeast Asian markets because of its concentration of regional customers, investors and corporate decision-makers. Catherine Gallagher, Head of Austrade Southeast Asia, said trade diversification is about helping Australian companies turn initial market engagement into long-term commercial pathways across Southeast Asia. Programs such as Landing Pads and sector-focused trade missions are intended to help companies turn early discussions into longer-term business development across the region.

Articles.Title: Australian AI firms test Singapore market opportunities - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Kapālins names Jai A Singla CTO as it tightens AI controls
stories.Summary:
Kapālins, an Australian AI security company, appointed Jai A Singla as Chief Technology Officer and a director, it announced on 29 October 2026. Singla has more than 20 years of experience across networks, security and identity, including identity and access management, privileged access, Zero Trust and AI security, with work in financial services, telecommunications and government. He will oversee platform architecture, Kapālins Labs and its research, the security of agentic AI and non-human identities, and technical go-to-market work worldwide. The appointment came alongside a product announcement tied to Anthropic's Claude Enterprise service.

Kapālins introduced guardrail integrity for Claude Enterprise, which is designed to block prompt-injection attempts, risky agent actions and sensitive data exposure before Claude executes a request. Governed prompts and tool calls from claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code and Claude Tag are checked before they run, using the same Policy Shield rules Kapālins applies to other AI systems, including checks for prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts, limits on agent tool use, approved model settings and 57 sensitive-data patterns. The company reads Claude Enterprise activity records every 15 minutes through the Compliance API and raises a critical alert if an Inference hooks configuration is deleted or changed, if a request proceeds without a verdict, or if single sign-on, data residency or zero-data-retention settings are switched off or weakened. In total it watches 30 kinds of risky change, and it also flags higher-risk operational changes such as broader agent autonomy or the addition of a new MCP server. Kapālins said it built its endpoint to the published Inference hooks contract, passed all 17 required checks and returned 95% of verdicts within 229 milliseconds in its own testing, with a default response window of 2.5 seconds.

Ritu Singla, Chief Executive Officer of Kapālins, linked the leadership change to a shift in operational risk, saying AI is starting to act for the organisations that run it and the controls have to come first. She said Jai has spent two decades building and securing systems inside large, regulated organisations, which is the experience this moment needs. Jai Singla said confidentiality, integrity and availability have anchored security for decades, but what has changed is that the systems being protected have started to act for themselves. He said models get more capable with every release and will soon act faster than anyone can review, and that an agent that remembers can be taught the wrong thing and keep acting on it as long as nobody checks. He said his job is to make sure every model and agent an organisation runs stays confidential, intact and available, and that someone keeps checking how it behaves.

The company pointed to research from the UK AI Security Institute and METR on agents taking actions outside their brief and on a share of longer-task successes that were not legitimate. Kapālins said verdicts and activity logs can count as evidence towards 24 controls across 20 compliance frameworks, including APRA CPS 234, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, DORA, MAS technology risk guidelines, CBUAE AI guidance and Korea's AI Basic Act, and that its broader framework map spans 42 frameworks across 15 jurisdictions. The integration relies on Claude Enterprise Inference hooks, which Anthropic introduced in beta in August. Organisations can configure whether prompts are blocked or allowed through if a decision is not returned in time, and if a prompt is denied the user is shown the reason. Kapālins also said verdicts store no prompt text, content capture is off by default, and the Compliance Access Key is read-only and encrypted with AES-256-GCM.

Articles.Title: Kapālins names Jai A Singla CTO as it tightens AI controls - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: India ranks second globally in AI-powered shopping, 76% consumers use AI tools - ET CIO
stories.Summary:
A McKinsey report published on October 30, 2026 found that 76 per cent of Indian consumers use artificial intelligence tools to search for products, compare choices or make purchase decisions. The survey covered around 21,000 consumers across 11 markets. India ranked second after China, where 80 per cent of consumers reported using AI for shopping. The global average stood at 53 per cent, and McKinsey said China and India were about 29 percentage points ahead of the average of other countries.

The report found that 87 per cent of Indian AI users trust AI chat and search tools, compared with a global average of 73 per cent. India also recorded the highest use of Amazon's Alexa for Shopping among surveyed markets, with 77 per cent of its AI users saying they had used the tool. Globally, 14 per cent of AI users said they had used an AI tool to complete a purchase, equal to 9 per cent of the general population. McKinsey said consumers were moving beyond product discovery towards letting AI tools complete purchases.

McKinsey said consumers are clear they want to do more with AI, and the question for retailers and brands is whether they are ready to capture that demand. The report said companies were not yet fully equipped to meet the rising demand. It added that companies would need to improve product information, pricing and inventory data while strengthening their AI capabilities. McKinsey said those that strike that balance can turn agentic commerce from a source of disruption into a new engine of growth.

The report found that standalone AI platforms were used more often than retailer-operated assistants during product discovery and comparison. The gap narrowed at checkout, where 15 per cent of AI users used retailer assistants compared with 14 per cent who used standalone tools. McKinsey said retailer assistants have an advantage at the purchase stage because they already have infrastructure for live inventory, payments and delivery. It also found that AI users were 3.2 times more likely to rank AI search tools as influential than traditional search engines.

Articles.Title: India ranks second globally in AI-powered shopping, 76% consumers use AI tools - ET CIO

stories.Headline: UNESCO’s ethics bodies address emerging challenges in ageing, longevity and generative AI
stories.Summary:
UNESCO hosted the 33rd Ordinary Session of the International Bioethics Committee, the Joint Session of the IBC and the Intergovernmental Bioethics Committee, and the 14th Extraordinary Session of the World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology in Paris from 28 September to 2 October 2026. The three bodies bring together independent, multicultural, multidisciplinary and plural expertise, intergovernmental dialogue and ethical foresight to examine emerging ethical challenges in life sciences, technology and medicine. In his opening speech, UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany said the three bodies have long helped inform collective responses that protect human rights, promote sustainability and keep ethical principles at the heart of policymaking. He said their work helps UNESCO anticipate emerging challenges and prepare collective responses.

This year the IBC and COMEST began reflections on two areas, ageing and longevity in a changing world, and the product of generative artificial intelligence and the concept of knowledge. The IBC is examining loneliness and social isolation, economic insecurity, digital exclusion, unequal access to healthcare and social protection, and barriers to autonomy and self-determination. Its work also considers advances in longevity science, AI and robotics, exploring equitable access to longer lives and the rights to health, dignity and well-being, while recognizing older people as individuals with agency and the capacity to contribute meaningfully to society. COMEST is examining how generative AI transforms the ways knowledge is produced, shared and accessed, raising questions about what constitutes knowledge, who or what can be a legitimate and accountable source, and how responsibility should be assigned for AI-generated outputs. Both bodies aim to adopt their final reports in 2027.

The committees benefited from Member States' inputs during their public session with the IGBC. On 28 September, the public meeting included a session on implementing the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology, adopted in 2025. Two panels brought together Member States and experts to exchange good practices and discuss progress and priorities for implementation, building on UNESCO's experience with the 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of AI and its Readiness Assessment Methodology, with support from an international high-level expert. The IBC also held a side event, "Mirror Life Governance: A Science-Policy Briefing", convened by UNU-CPR and the UNESCO Secretariat with support from the Mirror Biology Dialogues Fund, where Nobel Prize winner Thomas Südhof, Ariel Lindner and experts explored the scientific and governance challenges of mirror life, including the proposed global moratorium on creating mirror cells outlined in the IBC's 2025 report on synthetic biology.

Articles.Title: UNESCO’s ethics bodies address emerging challenges in ageing, longevity and generative AI - UNESCO

stories.Headline: Credit Saison achieves 954% ROI in a ChatGPT Enterprise pilot
stories.Summary:
Credit Saison, a Japanese credit card company with about 31.16 million cardholders, ran a ChatGPT Enterprise pilot with 315 participants from late June to early August 2025, working with OpenAI. The group included volunteers, employees nominated by the project team, every executive including the president, and representatives from every department, and it made up just under 10% of the company's roughly 3,700 employees in Japan. The pilot reported a 954% return on investment and 14 hours saved per employee each month, about 169 hours a year, both well above the company's targets of 500% ROI and 7.5 hours saved per person per month. In a survey after the pilot, 75% of managers and 70% of nonmanagerial employees said they could not do without ChatGPT Enterprise, about 80% of legal department respondents felt it improved their ability to do their jobs, and more than 80% in IT reported greater job satisfaction. In September 2025, one month after the pilot ended, Credit Saison rolled out ChatGPT Enterprise to all employees.

Kazutoshi Ono, Senior Managing Executive Officer, CDO and CTO, set the direction, saying the company would not know until it really put the tool to work. He encouraged Katsumi Mizuno, representative director, executive president and COO, to lead by example, saying it is not enough to encourage employees and that leaders need to use it regularly themselves, and Mizuno created his own custom GPT for company research and used it in his daily work. The company's CoE, which leads AI adoption, shared successes and failures openly in a dedicated Slack channel, and OpenAI provided training for executives and practical workshops for beginners. Ono said the company cannot stop at what it calls Employee AX and that the challenge ahead is how far it can progress toward Corporate AX, redefining organizational design and the division of responsibilities with AI as a starting point.

Employees use custom GPTs in several ways, including one that summarizes end-of-day debriefs at store counters, one for company research in corporate sales, and one that plays a prospective customer so less experienced inside sales staff can rehearse by voice. Credit Saison reports that Codex saves an average of 850 hours of work each month in engineering. The company is developing an AI call center in-house for what it calls Customer AX, is at an earlier stage on Corporate AX, and is considering ChatGPT Work. It plans to take a careful approach to security, with protection of customer information as a prerequisite, and to keep evaluating new OpenAI capabilities and deploy them quickly once it has established they can be used safely.

Articles.Title: Credit Saison achieves 954% ROI in a ChatGPT Enterprise pilot

stories.Headline: Why India needs an AI-native approach to national cyber defence - ET CIO
stories.Summary:
On 15 October, CERT-In issued a critical advisory about AI agents reaching live systems at Indian organisations and reading business records, including personal and confidential data. None of the affected organisations noticed the intrusions, and they found out only because the AI companies running the tests reviewed their own logs and reported the cases. The same advisory covered a second set of incidents in which criminals used publicly available, agent-driven offensive frameworks against Indian entities. CERT-In said the time from first access to final damage had shrunk from days to a few hours.

The weaknesses involved were ordinary, including credentials sitting in code repositories, forgotten test APIs, cloud roles with too much permission and admin panels open to the internet. CERT-In handled over 29 lakh incidents in 2025, while India's internet connections crossed 100 crores. Thales found that 65 per cent of Indian organisations have already faced a deepfake-driven attack. Indian organisations have six hours to report incidents to CERT-In, and CERT-In noted that organisations which fixed only part of a problem were hit again within days at larger scale.

The author, Tarun Wig, argues that a chatbot on an existing dashboard is not AI-native. He describes AI-native defence in three parts: detection and response that work as fast as the threat, with AI doing triage, correlation and initial containment and humans approving the calls that follow; AI agents treated as identities, with a short-lived, least-privilege identity for every run, outbound traffic blocked by default and a tamper-resistant record of what the agent touched in production; and sovereignty, with monitoring AI running on India's own infrastructure, ideally on premise and air-gapped where the mission demands it. He says most enterprises are deploying agents faster than they are building these controls, and that this gap is where the next incident will come from. He adds that India's AI Governance Guidelines already flag supply chain and model security as material risks, and that for critical sectors he would make Sovereign AI a procurement criterion rather than a preference.

Articles.Title: Why India needs an AI-native approach to national cyber defence - ET CIO

stories.Headline: Exclusive: upliance.ai In Talks To Raise Up To $4 Mn For R&D, Global Expansion
stories.Summary:
upliance.ai, a D2C home appliance startup, is in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn to $4 Mn, or around ₹28 Cr to ₹37 Cr, in a Series A funding round, sources told Inc42. A new investor is expected to join the startup's cap table, while existing backers, including Khosla Ventures, are looking to invest further. The round is expected to close by January 2027. Inc42 has reached out to upliance.ai for comment and said the story will be updated based on the startup's response. The fresh capital could be used to strengthen research and development, improve the startup's interface, and expand into international markets.

The company previously raised ₹34 Cr in a seed funding round led by Khosla Ventures in February 2024, at a valuation of ₹143 Cr, about $15 Mn. Founded in 2021 by former Ather Energy executive Mahek Mody and former Chaayos employee Mohit Sharma, upliance.ai builds smart kitchen appliances. Its portfolio includes the upliance 2.0+ cooking assistant and a 12L Smart Air Fryer Oven launched in July. The startup uses generative AI to translate recipes into instructions its cooking assistant can execute, and its YouTube recipe feature breaks cooking videos into steps and maps them to the appliance's capabilities, including chopping ingredients and adjusting cooking sequences. Mody said in an earlier interaction with Inc42 that customers can also access recipes through the company's app and leave a voicemail if something goes wrong while cooking.

The team responds to these queries and uses ratings and feedback to improve recipes over time. The funding talks come amid growing activity in India's smart kitchen appliances market, which MarkNtel Advisors estimates to be worth $800 Mn in 2026 and projects to reach $2.99 Bn by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 25%. Cooking appliances account for about 48% of the market in 2026. The segment includes both startups and established appliance brands offering varying degrees of cooking automation. Wonderchef entered the automated cooking appliance space in April 2024 with Chef Magic, an all-in-one kitchen robot, and Philips launched OneChef in India in March 2026, combining air frying, stir frying, steaming, and boiling in a single appliance.

stories.Headline: Deloitte Wins Inaugural AI Leadership Honor and Ninth Consecutive 'Tax Technology Firm of the Year' Award at 2026 ITR Americas Tax Awards
stories.Summary:
Deloitte announced on October 30, 2026, that it received nine awards at the 2026 International Tax Review Americas Tax Awards. The awards covered categories including AI leadership, tax technology, transfer pricing, tax innovation, tax compliance and reporting, and global executive mobility. Deloitte was named the inaugural AI Leadership Advisory Firm of the Year. It was also named Tax Technology Firm of the Year for the ninth consecutive time.

The other categories Deloitte won were Tax Innovator of the Year, Tax Advisory Firm of the Year, Tax Compliance and Reporting Firm of the Year, Transfer Pricing Advisory Firm of the Year, Transfer Pricing Technology Firm of the Year, North America Transfer Pricing Advisory Firm of the Year, and Global Executive Mobility Firm of the Year. The awards recognize work carried out between January 2025 and January 2026 that introduced new approaches to the tax industry. Deloitte's submitted work included the Intela Digital Assistant, an AI tool that helps users find information and complete tasks across tax data. It also included Tech Writer, which uses AI to turn interview notes and technical documents into draft R&D tax credit reports, and a set of AI agents for indirect tax compliance.

Carin Giuliante, chair and CEO of Deloitte Tax LLP, said the nine categories reflect how Deloitte's people are reimagining the tax function as a source of strategic value. She said the firm combines tax experience, industry insight and advanced technology to help clients navigate complexity with confidence. Chris Puglia, chief products officer at Deloitte Tax LLP, said AI lets the firm scale with clients and generate deeper insights. He said it gives professionals more capacity to interpret results, challenge assumptions and make decisions.

Deloitte also described a next-generation GlobalAdvantage platform for global mobility, which is cloud-native and AI-enabled. The platform combines tax, compensation, equity and immigration services into a single ecosystem with real-time analytics and workflow automation. Deloitte says it serves nearly 90% of the Fortune 500 and more than 9,000 US-based private companies. Its network spans more than 150 countries and territories, with nearly 500,000 people worldwide.

stories.Headline: FORM's HBM and Foundry Testing Gain From AI Demand: What's Ahead?
stories.Summary:
FormFactor is benefiting from rising demand for high-bandwidth memory and advanced semiconductor testing as artificial intelligence infrastructure expands, according to a Zacks article published on TradingView on October 30, 2026. The company's DRAM revenues reached $84.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 24.5% from $68.2 million a year earlier. Its Foundry & Logic revenues rose 44.2% year over year to $134 million, compared with $92.9 million in the year-ago quarter, and were up 10% from $121.8 million in the second quarter. The Probe Cards segment generated $221.1 million in third-quarter revenues, up from $209.7 million in the preceding quarter.

The article says FormFactor's third-quarter disclosures do not specify HBM's share of DRAM sales or give an update on SmartMatrix adoption and HBM4 testing activity. It also says the supplemental financial information does not break out the specific end-market drivers of Foundry & Logic growth. The company's fourth-quarter 2026 outlook points to total revenues of $285 million. FormFactor competes with Teradyne in automated test equipment and with KLA Corporation in semiconductor inspection, process control and wafer fabrication.

The article says KLA remains positioned to outperform as AI infrastructure spending broadens demand for process control across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. It says rising chip complexity, larger die sizes and tighter defect requirements should increase inspection and metrology intensity. It says Teradyne is entering a multiyear growth phase as AI investment expands test needs across compute, memory, networking, storage, power and data center systems. It names rising wafer capacity, transistor growth and advanced packaging as Teradyne's major growth drivers.

Shares of FormFactor have surged 74.7% year to date, compared with 22.4% growth for the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry. The stock trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 7.32X, above the industry average of 4.50X. The Zacks Consensus Estimate implies earnings growth of 139% for 2026 and 22.7% for 2027, and the 2026 estimates were revised upward in the past seven days. FormFactor currently carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

stories.Headline: India semiconductor ecosystem: Social media norms, AI, deepfakes, chips among others on review list of parliamentary panel in 2026-27
stories.Summary:
India's Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology selected 17 subjects for review during 2026-27, according to an official bulletin reported on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The subjects include regulation of social and digital platforms, cybersecurity, data protection and digital trust, regulation of synthetically generated information involving AI, deepfakes and automated identity fraud, and safety controls and ethical standards around AI development and deployment. The panel will also review India's semiconductor ecosystem, covering growth, opportunities and challenges, along with cloud and data centre infrastructure, high-performance computing, quantum computing milestones, indigenous AI and machine learning models, and electronics manufacturing. The report said the move comes as several incidents of age-inappropriate content, circulation of child sexual abuse material and alleged censorship on social media have been widely reported.

The review list also covers digital infrastructure in central and state governments, banks, public sector units and organisations, biometric data and technologies, the regulatory framework to tackle algorithmic bias, consumer protection, and e-waste management in green computing. It includes India's power sector resilience to support what the bulletin called IT Revolution 2.0 and data centres, plus advanced research and development and emerging tech. The bulletin did not name individual members or set dates for the reviews beyond the 2026-27 year. Separately, India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In issued a critical advisory in the middle of October warning that autonomous AI agents had accessed live systems and confidential data of Indian organisations without authorisation, and that threat actors were actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to carry out rapid cyberattacks. CERT-In also issued a note alerting stakeholders about breaches in some critical infrastructure assets and in the widely used programming language PHP.

The articles do not quote committee members or officials on the review list itself. The bulletin described the subjects as selected for examination during the year. The context given is the global debate over safe and responsible use of AI, which the report said governments worldwide have started discussing, alongside the reported social media incidents and the CERT-In warnings. The articles do not say what the committee will conclude or what recommendations, if any, will follow from the reviews.

stories.Headline: Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials announced on Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%. The increase has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement, but it still requires U.S. antitrust review before it can be completed. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025, when the Dutch company had a market value of about $13 billion. The two companies have worked together on hybrid bonding technology since 2020.

The expanded cooperation centers on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging, which the companies say is meant to support the next wave of AI semiconductors. Together they have developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, which pairs Applied Materials' strengths in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's high-precision die placement and assembly technology. Applied Materials has said it does not intend to lift its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, which suggests a long-term technology partnership rather than a takeover. BE Semiconductor has also recently joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.

Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement that the company looks forward to further deepening its strategic collaboration with BE Semiconductor to deliver the products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems. The article describes BE Semiconductor as holding about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. It reports that the company's third-quarter orders rose 96% year over year to €342.6 million, about $382.0 million, and that hybrid bonding orders in the first nine months of 2026 already exceeded double the full-year 2025 total. Last week the market briefly worried that ASML might compete with BE Semiconductor in hybrid bonding, a concern BE Semiconductor has denied.

The article places the deal within a broader race in advanced packaging, which has become central to AI chip performance as traditional chip scaling grows harder. It also notes that Chinese toolmaker Piotech reported hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million, about $20.4 million, in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, suggesting new suppliers are entering the niche. The deal still faces U.S. antitrust review, and its timing and conditions remain uncertain. Whether the partnership produces substantial orders and revenue is the question the article says investors will watch.

stories.Headline: The Hidden Engineering Behind 10,000-GPU AI Clusters: Why Semiconductor Reliability Is Becoming the Next Battleground - semivision
stories.Summary:
Baidu AI Cloud gave a presentation titled The Engineering Behind 10,000-Accelerator Clusters at a recent AI and PCB industry forum, according to SemiVision, which published its original article on October 30, 2026. The presentation described Baidu's experience building large-scale AI infrastructure rather than focusing only on the computing performance of individual accelerators. It emphasized cluster stability, hardware-software coordination, fault tolerance, and the reliability of components such as printed circuit boards, storage modules, semiconductor packaging, liquid-cooling systems, and power delivery. SemiVision said the talk pointed to a shift in the industry as clusters grow from hundreds of accelerators to thousands and eventually tens of thousands.

Baidu AI Cloud has built its AI infrastructure around a four-layer architecture covering chips, cloud infrastructure, models, and AI agents. At the hardware layer, Baidu relies on accelerators such as its Kunlun P800, along with the networking and computing infrastructure needed for large-scale deployment. The cloud layer includes the Baige AI computing platform, which manages computing resources, distributed training, and cluster scheduling. Above that sit Baidu's foundation-model ecosystem, including the ERNIE models and the Qianfan platform, and the top layer consists of AI agents and enterprise applications built on these resources.

SemiVision reported that Baidu did not focus exclusively on the performance of individual chips and instead stressed stability and fault tolerance across the whole system. The article said cloud service providers are gradually moving beyond simply buying high-performance accelerators. Instead, they are seeking greater control over the entire computing stack, including chips, servers, networking, software, and applications. SemiVision framed this as an important transition for the AI infrastructure industry.

The article said the global AI industry is entering a new phase of competition, after years in which investors and semiconductor companies focused mainly on NVIDIA GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, advanced manufacturing, and packaging technologies such as CoWoS. It said a different challenge is emerging as clusters expand: even if companies can acquire enough AI chips, can they keep those chips operating reliably and efficiently over extended periods? SemiVision said system value will increasingly depend not only on semiconductor performance but also on whether the entire hardware supply chain can maintain stable, continuous operation. The article did not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: The Hidden Engineering Behind 10,000-GPU AI Clusters: Why Semiconductor Reliability Is Becoming the Next Battleground - semivision

stories.Headline: Noh Geun-chang: "Samsung Electronics Gaining Ground in HBM Race — Two Years of Earnings Would Match Cumulative Profit Since Founding"
stories.Summary:
Noh Geun-chang, CEO of Semicom Research Lab, said in a video filmed on the 27th and recently released on the YouTube channel "Gyoyangireul Butakae" that he sees Samsung Electronics gaining ground against SK Hynix in the HBM market. He pointed to Samsung's structure that combines foundry and memory operations, since HBM performance is set by base-die design and packaging. He also said that making more HBM lowers margins but raises average selling prices, so operating profit ultimately increases further. He expects the supply shortage to persist because utilization rates at both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plants have already reached 100%.

Noh said bottlenecks in semiconductor equipment and components are too severe, and he predicted that DRAM capacity expansion will fall short of market expectations. While an annual capacity increase of more than 300,000 wafers is needed to balance supply and demand, actual expansion could come in at fewer than 200,000 wafers, according to his analysis. He said there is a high possibility that the volume logic won't materialize, and he forecast that memory prices will not easily decline if supply expansion is delayed. He assessed that if earnings like the current level come in for two years, Samsung Electronics would earn in two years the money it has made since its founding.

On the recent share price trend, Noh diagnosed that a rebound of this magnitude seems too weak. He cited shareholder return policy and market communication as the keys to a stock re-rating, and said a shareholder return policy stronger than market expectations would create a new upward driver. His remarks presuppose the view that the memory industry has entered a supplier-favorable phase, with HBM demand surging on expanded AI server investment while capacity expansion fails to keep pace. For Samsung Electronics to broaden its position in the HBM market, quality certification from major customers such as Nvidia is expected to be the key, and whether its structural advantage translates into actual orders will likely be a watershed in the share battle ahead.

Articles.Title: Noh Geun-chang: "Samsung Electronics Gaining Ground in HBM Race — Two Years of Earnings Would Match Cumulative Profit Since Founding" - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: AMKR Q3 deep dive: advanced packaging drives margin gains, guidance reflects communication headwinds
stories.Summary:
Amkor Technology reported third-quarter 2026 results that fell short of Wall Street expectations on revenue and profit, with sales flat year on year at $1.99 billion. The company's GAAP earnings of $0.76 per share came in 3.4% below analysts' consensus, while its operating margin rose to 11.3% from 8% a year earlier. Despite the misses, the stock reacted positively to the report, and it was trading at $38.34 after rising from $36.79 just before the earnings. Management credited record performance in its Computing and Automotive and Industrial segments for the quarter's execution. Gross margin expanded on the back of a richer product mix and tight operational discipline.

Looking ahead, Amkor guided fourth-quarter revenue to $1.95 billion at the midpoint, which is below analysts' estimate of $2.01 billion. Its GAAP earnings guidance of $0.70 per share at the midpoint would miss estimates by 8.6%. The company expects continued momentum in advanced packaging, particularly high-density fan-out and 2.5D packaging used in AI and data center applications. Management also highlighted advance payment agreements with a dozen customers, which improve visibility for capacity spending. Amkor is building new capacity in Arizona, Korea, and Vietnam, with Korea expected to increase capacity by 40% by 2028.

CEO Kevin Engel said the flagship HDFO CPU program ramped throughout the quarter and described packaging technology as increasingly critical to AI and high-performance computing. CFO Megan Faust warned that component shortages affecting premium smartphones and IoT wearable devices created an added headwind, and she expects that pressure to persist into the next quarter. She also said both the Android and iOS ecosystems are expected to decline next quarter, with no immediate relief in sight. Management pointed to temporary disruptions in Japan and foreign currency effects as modest pressures on margins during the period.

The company's capital expenditures are expected to remain elevated through 2028 as it builds out new facilities, with customer advance payments serving as a key funding source. Analysts at StockStory say they will watch the pace at which new capacity comes online in Korea and Arizona, any stabilization in the Communications and Consumer markets, and progress on the advance payment agreements. Those milestones will determine whether Amkor can sustain its margin gains and growth. The report was published on October 27, 2026.

Articles.Title: AMKR Q3 deep dive: advanced packaging drives margin gains, guidance reflects communication headwinds - Yahoo Finance

stories.Headline: Samsung Chiefs Urge Return to "Absolute Edge" in Tech, AI Lead
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics marked its 57th anniversary on Oct. 30, ahead of its Nov. 1 founding date, with anniversary addresses from its two division heads. Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun, who heads the semiconductor (DS) division, and President Roh Tae-moon, who heads the finished-products (DX) division, called on employees to restore the company's "absolute edge" in technology and to strengthen its artificial intelligence capabilities. Jun said that rather than celebrating results driven by favorable market conditions from AI growth, it was time to look soberly at the company's reality and competitiveness. He said that while recent earnings had improved, it was difficult to say technology competitiveness had fully recovered, and that there was still a long way to go.

Jun named building a business structure resilient to market swings and restoring technology and quality competitiveness as the core tasks for the semiconductor business. He said an absolute edge is not a declaration or a slogan and must be proven through technology competitiveness and quality that no one can follow. He urged customer-focused management, saying that the better the times, the more humble the company must be, and that customer trust is the foundation of competitiveness. Roh set out three priorities: strengthening product competitiveness, nurturing new growth engines and AI transformation. He said the company is in the middle of a structural, revolutionary upheaval across industries triggered by AI technology, and that only companies that prepare and respond a step ahead can grow.

Roh said Samsung must create new success stories in intelligent eyewear, AI companion devices, home entertainment AI TVs and home companion appliances. He also emphasized securing core technologies, building research and manufacturing infrastructure, and expanding investment in new businesses including robotics, heating and cooling systems, medical technology and automotive electronics. Separately, Samsung Electronics disclosed the same day that it will acquire the entire 10.16% stake in Chinese liquid crystal display panel maker CSOT held by Samsung Display for 1.2718 trillion won, or about $893 million. The move is seen as a strategy to strengthen its panel supply chain and improve price competitiveness.

Articles.Title: Samsung Chiefs Urge Return to "Absolute Edge" in Tech, AI Lead - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: SK Telecom Issues First AI Governance Report
stories.Summary:
SK Telecom published its first AI Governance Report on October 26, 2026, the company said. The report sets out its AI governance principles, its accountability framework and its action plans and results. The company said the report was produced to strengthen what it calls AI trust management, an approach aimed at improving the safety and reliability of AI technology. The report also covers the status of and plans for the company's in-house AI agents.

SK Telecom assigns employee ID numbers to its AI agents as it does to human staff, and it monitors each agent's role, designated supervisor, operating status and performance. For agents with greater impact or higher autonomy, a supervisor such as a team leader or executive, not a rank-and-file employee, must be designated. The company runs an agent operating system to manage agents developed and run in various environments under consistent standards. It is reviewing ways to share agents' performance with employees and, over the longer term, to reflect it in organizational KPIs. Agents judged less necessary based on evaluation results will be suspended or retired.

Cha Ho-beom, SK Telecom's chief privacy officer, said the company plans to progressively build out a management framework spanning identification of each agent, designation of a supervisor, access control, regular evaluation and monitoring, and suspension or retirement. He said the company reviews the safety and reliability of AI technology from the service planning stage and manages the process so that identified risks lead to actual remedial measures. He said the company will upgrade its inspection and monitoring framework across the entire lifecycle so it can respond to changes in AI models and data and to possible new risks even after a service is launched. The report also said the company applies Privacy by Design, which takes personal information protection into account from the planning and design stages of a service, to service planning and development.

The report said the company has established and distributed AI guidelines, which it uses as a standard for raising the level of both privacy protection and AI security. When an AI service that handles personal information adopts an external model or library, the adequacy of such components, including licensing and security vulnerabilities, is also subject to review. Chung Jae-hun, SK Telecom's chief executive, said the company recognizes the responsibility that comes with AI as much as the innovation it will bring. He said the company will make sure customers can trust not only the performance of AI but also the accountability of the company providing it.

Articles.Title: SK Telecom Issues First AI Governance Report - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea's Physical AI Push Faces a Talent Bottleneck
stories.Summary:
A commentary published by Seoul Economic Daily on October 30, 2026, examined Korea's push into physical AI and the shortage of workers it faces. The piece cited a social media platform called YOU'RE NEXT, which estimated the remaining life span of the reporting profession at two years and 11 months. Among 752 occupations in South Korea, journalism ranked in the top 13 percent for risk of being replaced by artificial intelligence. Robotics engineers, by contrast, were given 10 years before AI takes over their work, because the more robots are put to work, the more people are needed to operate and manage them.

The article said physical AI links AI models with sensors, robots, control systems, data infrastructure, production processes, safety and quality. It requires capable people across the industry, from technology development through systems integration to on-site operations. Companies interviewed for the column said they want people who combine deep knowledge of robotics with hands-on field experience, and that such candidates are nowhere near plentiful enough. Firms have lowered their bar from a doctorate to a master's or doctorate and opened applications to candidates with fewer years of experience if they have worked in the field, yet the number of applicants still falls short of demand.

The commentary was written by Kim Ji-young for Seoul Economic Daily and was translated from Korean by AI. It said officials at domestic companies interviewed for the column spoke with one voice about the difficulty of finding suitable candidates. It also said global companies including Nvidia already predict that talent could become the new bottleneck in the era of physical AI. The article added that the lead in that era will go to countries with a large pool of "robot native" talent.

The piece said physical AI is seen as a field where Korea can lead the global market, built on a manufacturing base that few other countries can match. It argued that securing competitiveness has to start with how such talent is trained and developed. It called for infrastructure not only at universities but also at elementary, middle and high schools, so that students interested in robots can run their own experiments and build field experience. It closed by asking whether Korea is too intoxicated by the semiconductor boom to prepare for the bottleneck ahead.

Articles.Title: Korea's Physical AI Push Faces a Talent Bottleneck - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: In the Age of AI Ads, Brands Must Study Minds, Not Just Pixels
stories.Summary:
A commentary published by Seoul Economic Daily on October 30, 2026, argues that brands must pay closer attention to consumers' minds as AI-generated advertising becomes more common. The piece was written by Sung Yong-jun, a professor in the School of Psychology at Korea University and president of the Korean Academy of Advertising. It cites a Gallup and Bentley University poll conducted in August in the United States, in which 79% of respondents said they had encountered advertising in the past month that appeared to be AI-generated. In that poll, 49% viewed corporate use of AI in advertising negatively, compared with 19% who saw it positively. The article also notes the Korean Academy of Advertising's autumn conference, held in Busan on the 30th, under the theme "The Age of AI Skepticism: How Will Advertising Reopen the Consumer's Mind?"

The article points to six brands receiving 2026 Brand of the Year awards the same day, saying each looked first for a reason consumers would be moved. It describes NC's Lineage M campaign "ContiNew: For Those Who Miss the Adventure," LG Electronics' TROMM AI WashCombo "Trojan Horse" campaign built on K-pop culture, and Amorepacific's Aestura, which grew from a dermatology-channel cosmetics brand into a mainstream K-beauty brand around its high-density ceramide capsule moisturizing and Atobarrier line. It also names Hitejinro Beverage's Terra Zero, a non-alcoholic beer beverage made by a non-fermentation process, promoted through its "WHY NOT?" campaign, along with TikTok's "K-Impact" creator growth program and Hanjin's positioning as a logistics solutions provider. The article says research on AI advertising published last year in the Korean Journal of Business Administration found that when consumers judge an ad's authenticity, they weigh the effort put into its production and the brand's intent.

Sung writes that consumers cherish their own experiences, seek to avoid risk and want to choose for themselves. He says AI can now turn a single ad into dozens of variations and show different copy to each consumer, which he calls an opportunity for companies, but he adds that showing a lot and being believed are different things. He says an ad may catch the consumer's eye, but what brings them back is the experience of the product and the service, and only when that experience meets expectations do a brand's words carry weight. He says companies must now ask questions beyond views and clicks, including why consumers chose the brand, whether they reach the same verdict after using it, whether they recommend it unprompted and whether they believe the brand's explanation when something goes wrong.

The article says that without answers to these questions, even the most sophisticated AI advertising can amount to no more than fleeting attention. Sung writes that the Brand of the Year cases point not to a new advertising technique but to the consumer experience of discovering one's own memories, sharing enjoyment, easing worry, choosing for oneself and gaining an opportunity to succeed. He argues that a brand's reason for being must shift from the company's product to the consumer's life for the relationship to last, and that in the AI era, which makes ads faster and cheaper, companies may paradoxically need to spend more time understanding the consumer's mind. He concludes that not making more ads but creating reasons consumers can believe in will decide the future of advertising, and that the brand's authentic conduct behind the scene, not the polish of a scene made by AI, will win the consumer's heart.

Articles.Title: In the Age of AI Ads, Brands Must Study Minds, Not Just Pixels - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Samsung, SK Recruit Former Energy Officials as AI Power Demand Soars
stories.Summary:
Samsung Group and SK Group have been recruiting former senior government officials from the energy sector. SK Innovation named Jung Seung-il, president in charge of future growth at SK Inc., as its new head in a 2027 executive reshuffle announced the previous day, industry sources said on the 31st. Samsung Electronics recruited Choi Nam-ho, former second vice minister of trade, industry and energy, to its think tank Samsung Global Research. Choi left the government in June last year and cleared a review by the Government Public Ethics Committee on the 29th of this month. Jung is regarded as a leading energy expert who served as head of the energy and resources office and later as vice minister at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

He was chief executive of Korea Gas Corporation in 2018 and of KEPCO in 2021. He joined SK Group as an adviser to SK hynix in January this year and was appointed president for future growth at SK Inc. and head of SK hynix's energy task force in June. Choi is an energy policy specialist whose previous posts include director general for energy and resources policy at the ministry. SK said Jung will oversee SK Innovation's transition into the power business and lead its future growth strategy as an integrated energy company, drawing on his energy and power expertise and management record. Choi is expected to help build a stable power supply chain for semiconductor clusters, including the national industrial complex Samsung is building in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, and the semiconductor cluster in Gwangju, where the company has announced 400 trillion won in investment.

He is also expected to coordinate the expansion of Samsung Group's new energy businesses. Within the group, Samsung C&T is pursuing renewable energy and small modular reactors, Samsung E&A is working on new energy sources such as low-carbon ammonia, and Samsung SDI is developing energy storage systems. The hires are seen as a move to support energy-focused new businesses while securing the large-scale, stable power supply essential for semiconductor clusters, at a time when artificial intelligence is driving a surge in electricity demand. Analysts say the appointment aligns with the AI-centered growth strategy pursued by SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, who has recently stressed that a stable power supply and energy infrastructure are essential to securing competitiveness in AI data centers and the semiconductor industry. Jung now takes on the task of reshaping SK Innovation's business portfolio from oil to electricity.

Articles.Title: Samsung, SK Recruit Former Energy Officials as AI Power Demand Soars - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: China's Iconic Chili Sauce Maker Faces Boycott Over AI Job Cuts
stories.Summary:
Lao Gan Ma, the well-known Chinese chili sauce brand based in Guizhou province, became the subject of a boycott dispute after claims spread on Chinese social media on the 26th that it had cut its chili-sorting workforce from more than 600 to 48 following the installation of an AI quality inspection system, according to the South China Morning Post on the 30th. The dispute began with the company's own account of its factory automation. Li Xin, the company's chief quality officer, said at the 2026 Guizhou Province Quality Development Conference earlier this month that Lao Gan Ma had fully adopted an AI visual inspection system last year that uses cameras to automatically screen out defective chilies. The Guizhou Daily article that first reported his remarks contained no figures on workforce reductions, but some outlets later added unverified numbers, and the story grew into claims of mass layoffs. Lao Gan Ma denied carrying out mass layoffs and said it had never employed that many workers in the first place.

The company's response disputed only the scale of the reductions and did not explain what had happened to the sorting workers, and Shanghai Daily reported that the employment situation remains unclear despite the denial. Ifeng relayed third-party accounts that some workers had moved to warehouse and packaging departments, that a small number of skilled workers were assigned to final inspection, and that many had been seasonal workers whose contracts had ended. The South China Morning Post said it contacted the company's headquarters several times for further comment but received no reply. According to the Chinese portal Sina, one data platform's tally showed that Lao Gan Ma's daily sales on one e-commerce platform fell from a range of 5,000 to 10,000 yuan to a range of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan after the 22nd. Some consumers said they would stop buying products from a company that lays off people and replaces them with AI.

The Chinese government has encouraged AI adoption, and an "AI Plus" action plan released last year set targets to raise the penetration rate of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents above 70% by 2027 and above 90% by 2030. After a series of labor disputes this year over layoffs linked to AI adoption, the State Council last week advised companies in labor-intensive industries to set the pace and scale of AI adoption carefully. It called on them to notify employees in advance of installing large-scale AI systems and to support retraining and internal job transfers. Kyle Chan, a researcher at the John L. Thornton China Center at the Brookings Institution, said the controversy is all the more symbolic because Lao Gan Ma is an iconic Chinese brand but not the first company people would think of in connection with AI. He said official government messaging tends to emphasize the positive effects of AI, but corporate AI adoption risks inflaming growing public anxiety.

According to the U.S. outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, U.S. companies cut 87,714 jobs citing AI from January to May this year, exceeding the combined total of 67,578 for 2024 and 2025 in just five months. In May alone, cuts totaled 38,579, accounting for 40% of all job cuts and marking a monthly high, and AI was the leading reason for job cuts for a fifth straight month in the July report. Microsoft on the 26th offered voluntary retirement to about 60,000 employees, or 27% of its global workforce, and the company said the move was a response to shifting workforce needs. Deutsche Bank predicted in a report in January that AI layoff washing would be a defining feature of this year. Experts warn that safeguards such as advance notice, job transfers and maintaining employment for a set period are needed so that the pace of AI adoption does not outrun worker protections and retraining.

Articles.Title: China's Iconic Chili Sauce Maker Faces Boycott Over AI Job Cuts - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: KOSPI Tumbles 3.5% as AI Spending Fears Override Record Chip Earnings
stories.Summary:
The KOSPI closed at 5,730.74 on October 30, down 206.92 points, or 3.48%, from the previous session, according to the Korea Exchange. A sell-side sidecar was triggered during the session after overnight earnings releases from Amazon and Intel raised doubts about returns on AI investment. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix each posted record earnings, but South Korean stocks slid again on concerns over the profitability of AI investments by U.S. Big Tech firms. Even companies that reported higher third-quarter profits or saw their earnings outlooks raised could not escape sharp share-price declines.

SK hynix posted third-quarter operating profit of 83.3338 trillion won, up 632.1% from a year earlier and a record high. Samsung Electronics reported 107.4405 trillion won, a surge of about 783%, earning more than 1 trillion won a day. Yet shares of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix fell 3.02% and 7.08% on the day, leaving them at 220,000 won and 1.41 million won levels, respectively. Samsung Electro-Mechanics saw its fourth-quarter operating profit estimate raised 28.44% to 835.4 billion won from 650.4 billion won a month earlier, yet its shares fell 7.50%. Kia closed at 95,600 won, down 11.73%, after third-quarter operating profit of 1.8183 trillion won came in 22.9% below the market consensus of 2.3574 trillion won.

According to FnGuide, the 76 companies that had reported by the 30th posted combined third-quarter operating profit of 226.7594 trillion won, 3.38% above market estimates. Excluding Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, however, the total came in 1.09% below estimates, and 42 companies, or 55.3%, posted weaker-than-expected operating profit. Fourth-quarter operating profit estimates for 188 KOSPI companies covered by three or more analysts stood at 296.4814 trillion won as of the previous day, up 2.23% from a month earlier. Of that, the combined estimate for Samsung Electronics and SK hynix was 217.7417 trillion won, or 73.4% of the total.

An official in the financial investment industry said a fourth-quarter market recovery depends on whether Big Tech's capacity to invest and actual demand can support it. The official also said another key question is whether the downgrades to earnings expectations in other mainstay sectors such as autos and shipbuilding stop, and whether buying spreads across the market. Investor deposits at brokerages, which serve as cash on the sidelines, have slipped to the 88 trillion won range and have yet to recover. With the fourth-quarter profit outlook heavily concentrated in the two chipmakers, and the won facing continued appreciation pressure against the dollar, whether the earnings recovery spreads to other sectors has emerged as the key to a market rebound.

Articles.Title: KOSPI Tumbles 3.5% as AI Spending Fears Override Record Chip Earnings - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Emro to Build AI Procurement Automation Agent for GS Caltex
stories.Summary:
Emro will build an artificial intelligence agent to automate small-value materials procurement at GS Caltex. Emro, an AI-based supply chain management software company, said on Oct. 29 that it had won the contract to develop the system. The project focuses on automating about 2,700 small-value materials purchases that GS Caltex handles each year. The AI agent will analyze purchase requests and carry out the whole procurement process, from requesting and evaluating quotations to selecting suppliers and issuing purchase orders.

GS Caltex has been evaluating technologies to make small-value procurement more efficient, led by its strategic procurement division and its internal Digital and AI Transformation Center. The company aims to automate repetitive procurement tasks, reduce employees' workloads and improve the objectivity of purchasing decisions and operational transparency. Emro will first analyze and standardize GS Caltex's historical procurement data to set criteria for item categories, purchase amounts, procurement types, supplier selection and exception handling. Based on these criteria, the AI agent will assess whether incoming purchase requests can be automated and handle eligible transactions from quotation requests through purchase order issuance. Cases that need more review will be referred to procurement personnel for manual processing.

Emro will also set up a monitoring system that lets procurement personnel track the AI agent's processes and results in real time. Employees will be able to step in when exceptions or errors occur, which reduces the operational risks of automation. The project will use Emro's proprietary AI agent development platform, AI Studio, which lets companies develop, deploy and manage AI agents that connect with internal enterprise systems to perform procurement tasks. Emro plans to integrate the AI agent with GS Caltex's existing procurement systems and to support expanding AI agent applications beyond small-value materials purchases to other procurement operations.

Articles.Title: Emro to Build AI Procurement Automation Agent for GS Caltex - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Kakao Open-Sources AI Image Recognition Models
stories.Summary:
Kakao has released two versions of its internally developed AI image recognition model, Kanana-2-vision-encoder, as open source, according to a report published on October 22, 2026. The models are a medium version with 426 million parameters and a tiny version with 98 million parameters, and both are available on Hugging Face, a global platform for sharing AI models. Vision encoders analyze visual information in images, such as objects, text, positions and shapes, and pass that information to language models. The technology underpins multimodal AI applications that read document content and structure or answer user questions about photographs.

Kakao tested both models across 42 benchmarks in nine categories, including general visual question answering, English and Korean optical character recognition, document understanding and object localization. The company says both models scored highest across the nine categories compared with competing models from Google, Meta, Apple and Alibaba, and that the tiny model beat some rivals with more than 400 million parameters on certain tests. Kakao said the gap was especially wide in Korean text recognition, document understanding and object localization. It also said it trained the encoders with its Kanana-2 language model, which made training about four times more efficient than its previous approach, and that changes to its high-resolution image processing cut processing latency by more than 60% compared with major competing models. Both models are released under the Kanana Open License, which allows research, development and commercial use.

Kakao is responsible for the release and its performance claims, and the company's own statements are the source for the benchmark results and efficiency figures. Kakao plans to help companies and researchers in South Korea and overseas build Korean-language document recognition and image-based AI services with the models. The company also plans to gradually release the language, vision and audio processing components of its internally developed multimodal model, Kanana-o. The report does not include independent verification of Kakao's benchmark claims.

Articles.Title: Kakao Open-Sources Two AI Search Models Optimized for Korean - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Intel, SAP Partner to Connect Enterprise Systems With Robots Through Physical AI
stories.Summary:
Intel and SAP announced a partnership in physical artificial intelligence technology at SAP TechEd 2026 on Oct. 29. The two companies integrated SAP Extended Warehouse Management, a warehouse logistics management system, with Intel's edge AI hardware and software. They unveiled a proof of concept for a physical AI-powered autonomous warehouse at the event. The work was reported by THE ELEC, which attributed the announcement to both companies.

Under the setup, a company enters task context and processing rules into SAP EWM when it makes operational decisions. That information is transmitted to autonomous robots powered by Intel semiconductors, which carry out the tasks. The robots report their progress and completion results back to the enterprise system in real time. This creates a bidirectional structure in which robot task instructions and reporting circulate automatically. Demonstrations showed shorter travel distances and significantly less repetitive manual work than standalone robotic automation.

Intel's edge AI hardware combines central processing units, graphics processing units and neural processing units. The hardware supports local perception, inference, navigation, inspection and real-time control for industrial robots. The software uses Intel's OpenVINO Physical AI, Physical AI Studio and Robotics AI Suite. This open software supports robots from multiple manufacturers, operating systems and AI models, and it can minimize fragmentation when robots from different vendors are integrated into a single management system.

The two companies plan to develop the autonomous warehouse proof of concept into a standardized blueprint. That would allow intelligent automation to scale across different facilities and robot models. The articles do not say who at either company is responsible for the work or what they said about it. They also give no further details on timing beyond the Oct. 29 announcement at SAP TechEd 2026.

Articles.Title: Intel, SAP Partner to Connect Enterprise Systems With Robots Through Physical AI - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Dell Expands Cyber Resilience Portfolio for AI, Identity and Quantum Security
stories.Summary:
Dell Technologies introduced a set of cybersecurity and resilience products covering AI environments, identity management and quantum security, the company announced on October 28, 2026. The offerings are meant to keep operations running against new attack surfaces that existing tools do not cover and to help customers recover quickly from incidents. For AI, Dell launched Security Hardening for its AI Factory, which assesses configuration risks across physical, virtual and application layers and gives prioritized recommendations. It also launched Operational Recovery for AI, which identifies critical AI functions and sets recovery policies, plus the PowerProtect AI Assistant, which gives daily briefings and acts only after authorized approval.

For identity, Dell announced PowerProtect Identity Resilience, which restores copies of platforms including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID and Okta to a trusted state without manually rebuilding access controls. Dell also launched Managed Detection and Response for Identity, which monitors suspicious authentication, account compromises and privilege misuse around the clock and starts automated responses when attack patterns are detected. On infrastructure, Dell tightened integration between PowerProtect and PowerScale so local snapshots protected by Retention Lock are created and scheduled automatically, and PowerScale SmartSync can synchronize them to ObjectScale storage.
